subject: Weekly staff trajectory brief: wins, impediments, and QBR readiness
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Anya Petrova <anya@orbitai.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly staff trajectory brief: wins, impediments, and QBR readiness

Team —

Quick weekly pulse ahead of next week's QBR. High-level readout (keeps short so exec distro can scan):

Wins
- Hosted API: Latency P50 improved by ~11% after kernel patch; customer-facing demo this morning with OrbitAI went smoothly.
- Dedicated rollout: First Dedicated cluster hit committed throughput for 48h during internal soak.
- Telemetry: Console now surfaces per-route token costs for top 5 customers (initial rollout to internal beta).

Risks / Impediments
- SLA exception request from OrbitAI: they are asking for a 99.9% p95 latency SLA for a narrow traffic window; current Dedicated config is borderline. Need a decision on short-term capacity bump vs. controlled SLA carve-out.
- QBR pack is missing consolidated ask on Support headcount; we need a one-paragraph rationale and the number by EOD Thursday.
- Security artifacts: OrbitAI asked for two additional logs for their audit — we can provide them but it requires a short retention-policy exception for that customer.

Asks (action items)
- Laura: please confirm whether exec is comfortable granting a 30-day capacity bump for OrbitAI (we'll bill overtime) or whether we should propose a tiered SLA with fallbacks. Need a yes/no by 5pm PT today.
- Karthik: update the QBR spreadsheet (sheet named "Support Ask") with the headcount ask + cost delta. Send me the updated link.
- Marissa: please draft a short memo (2–3 bullets) for Legal/Security outlining the retention exception and controls; I can route to Security if you want me to.

Attachments: QBR_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook + timeline), OKR_checkpoint_sheet.csv (current objective progress).

Notes: OrbitAI demo scheduled for 11:00 PT today — Anya is cc'd for visibility. If we grant a temporary capacity uplift, DevOps will need the order by 10:30 to validate capacity.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Operations
Redwood Inference

---
[Attachment stubs: QBR_runbook_v1.pdf (13 pages), OKR_checkpoint_sheet.csv (spreadsheet)]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Anya Petrova <anya@orbitai.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly staff trajectory brief: wins, impediments, and QBR readiness

Tessa — thanks for the crisp readout. Quick replies: 

- OrbitAI SLA: I agree we should avoid a hard 99.9% commitment for p95 without a capacity plan. Approve 30-day capacity bump for their traffic window contingent on cost reimbursement and a short-term rollback plan. I'll OK it now and ask Finance to prepare a one-page amendment.

- Support headcount: I'm inclined to support +2 ICs for incident coverage during QBR ramp, but need the cost delta in the sheet before I sign off. Karthik, can you fill that in by EOD?

- Retention exception: route the memo through Legal + Security. Marissa, please cc me when you send it.

Also — Laura notes: can we schedule 30 mins in the QBR dry-run to walk the OrbitAI carve-out and rollback plan? Suggest 4:30 PT today.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
